message.content:
Sure! If your DNS‑management provider exposes its CAA record data through a **REST** interface, most APIs let you specify exactly which fields you want back so you don’t have to download everything.  
Below is a quick guide – replace `https://api.yourdnsprovider.com` with whatever base URL your service uses.

---

### 1️⃣ Build the Request URL  

```
GET https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/{domain}/records/Caa
```

* `{domain}` → `sample2.com`

Add a *query parameter* called `fields`, listing comma‑separated field names you care about. In this case we only want the unique identifier (`id`) and the contextual metadata (`context_attributes`).  

Full path becomes:

```
/v1/domains/sample2.com/records/Caa?fields=id,context_attributes
```

> ⚠️ Some providers may name the attribute differently; check the docs for exact spelling (e.g., `ctx_attrs`, `metadata`, …).

---

### 2️⃣ Add Authentication Header  

Your API key goes into the HTTP header. Most services expect it as a bearer token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

If they require a custom header (like `X-API-Key:`), swap accordingly.

---

### 3️⃣ Example Using `curl`

```bash
curl \
    --request GET \
    --url "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records/Caa?fields=id,context_attributes" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer secret567"
```

#### Expected Response (JSON)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "caa12345",
      "context_attributes": { ... }
    },
    {
      "id": "caa67890",
      "context_attributes": { ... }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_count": 2,
    "_links": { /* optional */ }
  }
}
```

Only the two requested properties appear inside each object—no other CAA details are sent over the wire.

---

### 4️⃣ Alternative: Use Query Parameters Instead of Body

Some APIs allow you to pass the same filter list in the request body when doing a `POST`. That’s handy if you’re working within a UI framework that prefers bodies over URLs.

Example payload:

```json
{
  "filter_fields": ["id", "context_attributes"]
}
```

Send it as part of a `POST` to `/v1/domains/sample2.com/records/Caa/query`.

---

### 5️⃣ Pagination & Rate Limits

Even though you’re requesting fewer fields, there might still be many CAA records. Check whether the response includes paging links (`next_page_url`, `prev_page_url`) or cursor tokens. Respect any rate limits indicated in headers (`x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`).

---

### 6️⃣ Quick Checklist Before You Run It

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✔︎ | Replace `https://api.yourdnsprovider.com` with your actual domain. |
| ✔︎ | Verify the correct field names (`id`, `context_attributes`). |
| ✔︎ | Confirm authentication method (Bearer vs X‑API‑Key). |
| ✔︎ | Test against a sandbox environment first. |

Once you hit “Run”, you’ll receive a lean JSON containing only what you asked for—greatly reducing bandwidth and parsing overhead!

Let me know if you’d prefer a different programming language example (Python, JavaScript, Go…) or if you run into any hiccups while testing. Happy coding!
